Let me analyze this conflict.

Axis: applicant
- Register: "MinebeaMitsumi Inc."
- Document: "Minebea Co., Ltd."

This is interesting. Minebea Co., Ltd. is the historical name of the company that later became MinebeaMitsumi Inc. (after merging with Mitsumi Electric in 2017). The certificate is from 2011, so at the time of issuance, the legal entity was "Minebea Co., Ltd." The register says "MinebeaMitsumi Inc." which is the current name of the company (possibly the register was updated to reflect the current corporate name, or an extraction error).

Is this "same-entity" under the rules? The rules say: "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity." "MinebeaMitsumi Inc." vs "Minebea Co., Ltd." — these are not just spelling/suffix drift; they're different corporate names entirely (one includes "Mitsumi"). However, they refer to the same corporate entity across a name change. The rule "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

Hmm. Is "MinebeaMitsumi Inc." vs "Minebea Co., Ltd." a "genuinely different company name"? From a strict name-matching perspective, yes — they are different names. But historically they denote the same legal entity (renamed). The question asks to decide the relationship.

Given the rules as stated, the decision categories are: same-entity (drift), document-noise, different-entity (genuinely different names), unverifiable. The register value could be a later modernization of the applicant name (the OIML-CS database may have updated the company name after the merger). But per the rules, since these are genuinely different company names (not mere spelling/suffix drift), the verdict would be "different-entity" with best_value = document's "Minebea Co., Ltd.", because the certificate is the legal instrument and at issuance the company was named Minebea Co., Ltd.

Alternatively, one could argue same-entity because they refer to the same company over time. But the rule for same-entity is limited to spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences. "MinebeaMitsumi Inc." is not a spelling variant of "Minebea Co., Ltd." — the "Mitsumi" token is added. So different-entity is the correct verdict per the given rules.

Best value: the document's "Minebea Co., Ltd." since the certificate is the legal instrument and reflects the name at issuance.

Why: one short sentence: "The 2011 certificate names the applicant as it existed at issuance (Minebea Co., Ltd.); 'MinebeaMitsumi Inc.' is a later renamed entity, so the legal instrument's name governs."
